DFMA Review · S7 cost drivers, report and PDF · mock-up of a screen change · 8 Nov 2026

Export PDF and cost drivers

The answer: the screen gets an Export PDF button and a short, closed list called Cost drivers: a ranked list of what makes this part costly to make (more setups, more tools, deep holes, sharp corners). It shows counts only, no hours or dollars.

What the PDF holds: page 1 gives the verdict in one line, then the part's size, the machine and its steps exactly as the screen shows them (the raw bar or block, the numbered tool steps), the tools, how many times a tool is loaded, and the cost drivers. Each finding then gets its own page, with a picture of the part and the finding's faces in blue. The assumptions come last.

Your call

Approve, Change (say what), or Rethink.

One question inside this: the ranked list has no entry for deep pockets, undercuts or long thin shafts (the spec's list came before them). I added deep bores only. Should I add those three as cost drivers? My pick: yes.

Try it in the demo: tap report_sample, open Cost drivers, tap Export PDF. The demo cannot save the PDF: the viewer blocks every download, so Export PDF only works in the app on a computer. The two PDF pages below are renders of a real export.

For the record: where each fact comes from

  • PDF contents (first page, then a section and an image per finding): docs/specs/first-version.md:97-102 (J6).
  • Cost drivers: count × weight, only counts above 0, high score first then key A to Z, no time or dollars: docs/specs/first-version.md:322-336 and D-003; weights and labels in config/drivers.toml, all 1.0 and labelled estimate.
  • Plan text on screen and in the PDF is the same code (web/src/findings.ts): stock, numbered operations, D-029 rough and finish tools as separate loads (docs/DECISIONS.md D-029).
  • Mapping to the new rules (my default, not yet approved): bore_depth counts as a deep hole; turn_offaxis as off-axis; access as 4/5-axis. pocket_depth, undercut, turn_slender, looks_turned and turn_axis feed no driver, because the spec's list has none for them.
  • Test part sizes and findings: tests/parts/make_parts.py (report_sample).
